title: Collateral Department Note: Land Mix of the Parcels Staying Mortgaged and the Post-Split Limit — Farm Real Estate Loans
content:
When a member asks to split the farmstead out of a Farm Real Estate Loans mortgage, the post-split limit follows what stays mortgaged: when pasture and recreational land make up more than 30 percent of the value that stays mortgaged, it is 5.0 points lower; when irrigated cropland makes up at least 60 percent of that value and pasture and recreational land 30 percent or less, it is 5.0 points higher; otherwise it is not changed.

**Measuring what stays mortgaged.** The value that stays mortgaged is the appraised value of the parcels still mortgaged (every parcel mortgaged to the loan less every parcel released from it) less the homesite, the parcel of land use farmstead still mortgaged. Each land use's value is the appraised value of its parcels mortgaged less those released; pasture and recreational land are counted together.

## Ladder

| Pasture and recreational land, share of what stays | Irrigated cropland, share of what stays | Change to the post-split limit |
|---|---|---|
| more than 30 percent | any | 5.0 points lower |
| 30 percent or less | 60 percent or more | 5.0 points higher |
| 30 percent or less | less than 60 percent | no change |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical, value that stays mortgaged USD 750000)

| Pasture and recreational | Irrigated cropland | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 225000 (exactly 30 percent) | 450000 (exactly 60 percent) | 5.0 points higher |
| 225001 | 450000 | 5.0 points lower |
| 150000 | 449999 | no change |
| 0 | 750000 | 5.0 points higher |
